message.content:
The exact number of mitochondria varies widely depending on the cell type and its metabolic demands. In most mammalian cells you’ll find:

| Cell type | Typical range of mitochondria per cell |
|-----------|----------------------------------------|
| Neurons (high energy demand) | **~10 000–100 000** |
| Muscle cells (especially cardiac) | **~5 000–50 000** |
| Liver hepatocytes | **~1 000–10 000** |
| Epithelial cells | **~200–2 000** |
| Immune cells (e.g., macrophages) | **~500–5 000** |

So while a single mitochondrion is a tiny organelle (~0.5–1 µm), a typical human cell contains **hundreds to tens of thousands** of them, depending on its function.
